correctness.rationale: For every fixed a,b>0 the second fixed-point equation G(x,y)=y-sin^2(b*pi*y+a*x)=0 has G_y(0,0)=1, yielding a unique small analytic graph Y(x)=a^2*x^2+2*a^3*b*pi*x^3+O(x^4). The phase theta=a*pi/x+b*Y(x) has theta'=-a*pi/x^2+O(x) strictly below -alpha' for alpha=arcsin(sqrt(x)); the two equations theta=n*pi+/-alpha each cross once in every sufficiently high band. Taylor substitution proves x_{n,+/-}=a/n -(+/-)a^(3/2)/(pi*n^(5/2))+O(n^-7/2), y=a^4/n^2+O(n^-3), and N(epsilon)=2a/epsilon+O(1). Direct Jacobian trace/eigenvalue scale gives lambda_unstable=-sigma*2*pi*n^(3/2)/sqrt(a)+O(n^1/2), lambda_stable=2*a^2*b*pi/n+O(n^-2), opposite determinant signs. Independent scipy root searches with a=b=1 at n=30,80,150 for each sign confirmed positions, both residuals and real saddle signs. Finite tests corroborate; analytic monotonicity supplies the all-n conclusion.
